brief.headline: Lock ₹0.65–0.80/pc price on our main cap SKU (market shows headroom below typical ₹0.85–0.95), and qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek as second source—we have five credible alternates.

priceAsk.summary: Push our cap price down to the ₹0.65–0.80/pc range at higher volume or with looser specification.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc for the 28 mm induction-wad PP cap
priceAsk.basis: The market asking price for this cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec—so we are targeting the lower end of that headroom band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask them to move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Cutting 15 days frees up ₹2.77 L of cash for us.

brief.financialLeverage: Empire Industries publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. Our ₹67.47 L annual spend is meaningful but not huge for a listed firm. Without financial transparency, we push on price and terms by showing we have strong alternates lined up—Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) and Mold-Tek (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100)—and can shift volume if they don't move.

evidence.point: The open market for our main cap (28 mm induction-wad PP cap) shows room to move down to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec.
evidence.figure: askBand ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80

evidence.point: We spend ₹67.47 L a year with them—a meaningful chunk of business they will want to keep.
Pulling payment back by 15 days frees up ₹2.77 L in cash for us.
We have five qualified alternates already identified, including Manjushree (India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100).
Mold-Tek is a listed, profitable rigid-plastic leader with ₹1010.97 Cr revenue and health B 73/100—a robust second source for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr, health B 65/100), direct fit for pharma bottles and caps—top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100), strong and profitable—a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging specialist (₹701.17 Cr, health C 51/100), broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Empire publishes no financials—we can't gauge their cash position or stability, so monitor delivery reliability closely if we push hard.
The market ask verdict says MARKET-FAIR—we're not wildly overpaying now, so the price cut will require real volume commitment or spec flexibility on our side.
Our ₹67.47 L spend is significant but not massive for a listed firm; if they see us as a smaller customer, they may dig in—use the alternates to show we will move volume.
Qualifying a new supplier (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) takes time—kick off the second-source process now so we have real leverage in 90 days.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're seeing market prices for caps like ours in the ₹0.65–0.80 range at higher volume—and we've started qualifying Manjushree and Mold-Tek as second sources to ensure we're getting the best deal.
